meta.name: SpendSight Dashboard Design Language
meta.description: High-level design and style guidelines derived from a modern financial analytics dashboard. This file is intended to guide AI-generated UI so that new screens visually match the reference layout and style.
design_goals: Feel like a professional financial institution dashboard: trustworthy, calm, and data-focused.
Use clean, minimal surfaces with clear hierarchy and plenty of whitespace.
Prioritize readability of numbers, trends, and time-series data.
Keep the interface neutral and cool, with subtle use of color for emphasis rather than decoration.

grid.behavior: Use a centered, fixed-width content area inside the viewport. Align cards and charts to an implicit 12-column grid. Do not stretch content edge-to-edge; always preserve generous outer margins.

app_shell.structure: Three main zones: left vertical sidebar, main content grid, and top-level browser chrome simulated by the mockup.
app_shell.max_page_width_behavior: Center the dashboard content area while the sidebar remains flush with the left edge.
app_shell.scrolling_behavior: Sidebar is fixed; main content scrolls vertically under the top header area if present.

sidebar.border: Right-hand subtle divider line using color.border.subtle.
sections: Logo and app name at the top with generous padding.
Search field under logo, full width.
Primary navigation section (Performance, Financial Ventures, etc.) with vertical list of items.
Secondary navigation or utility items grouped lower.
User profile/footer block at the very bottom with avatar, name, and email.

nav_item.icon_alignment: Icon on left, label next, optional right-aligned pill or chevron.
nav_item.inactive_style: Neutral text color (color.text.muted) on transparent background. Icon in color.icon.muted.
nav_item.active_style: White or near-white background, subtle rounded rectangle or pill, accent-colored left stripe or dot, label in color.text.primary with medium weight.
nav_item.hover_style: Slightly darker background than sidebar, maintain same spacing and alignment.

content.behavior: Compose the dashboard from multiple cards arranged in a 12-column grid. Cards should align to rows and maintain consistent vertical rhythm.

usage.card_inner_padding: Use spacing.5 (20px) on all sides for standard cards. For dense summaries, allow spacing.4 on secondary rows.
usage.between_sections: Use spacing.7 or greater to visually separate logical groups of cards.
usage.form_field_gap: Use spacing.4 between label and input, spacing.4–spacing.5 between stacked fields.
usage.table_row_padding: Vertical padding equivalent to spacing.3 inside table rows.

usage.button: Use radius.md for standard buttons, radius.pill for pills and badges.
usage.input: Use radius.md for inputs and search fields.
usage.chart_container: Match the hosting card radius for consistency.

usage.card: Default to elevation.1 to subtly lift cards from the canvas.
usage.hovered_card: Optionally increase to elevation.2 with a slight scale-up for emphasis.
usage.floating_elements: Use elevation.2 for modals or floating panels when introduced.

guidelines: Use the canvas and subtle background colors to create a soft, low-contrast frame around white cards.
Reserve the primary green (color.green.500) for success states, key numbers, active navigation, and positive trend indicators.
Use the blue scale (color.blue.*) for CTAs, key links, or highlighted modules.
Use purple tones sparingly for secondary emphasis, tags, or comparison series in charts.
Use orange and red scales for caution and error states respectively, limiting their use to status indicators and alerts.
Text should predominantly use neutral scale values (color.neutral.700 and below), with muted text for helper copy and labels.
Charts should be mostly monochrome (neutral scale) with one or two accent hues from blue, green, or purple for emphasis rather than a rainbow palette.

font_family.primary: Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif
font_family.numeric: Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif
font_family.usage: Use the same geometric sans-serif for body and numerics to maintain a clean, modern aesthetic. Ensure tabular numbers are used in key financial tables if supported.

display.xl.usage: Hero headlines, major section titles (rare use).

display.md.usage: Panel headers or hero metrics titles.

heading.lg.usage: Major card headers and section dividers.

heading.xs.usage: Small labels within cards (e.g., metric labels, sub-section headings).

body.lg.usage: Larger body text for emphasis or readability.

body.md.usage: Primary body copy in cards and labels.

body.sm.usage: Secondary copy, helper text, data labels.

body.xs.usage: Tiny labels, captions, chart axis labels.

numeric.md.usage: Key metrics within cards (e.g., percentages, dollar amounts).

guidelines: Use stronger weights (600–700) for titles and key metrics; keep the rest of the interface at regular weight for a calm, professional feel.
Do not use overly large display sizes on this dashboard; keep type compact and information-dense while preserving readability.
Maintain consistent letter spacing and line heights to avoid a cramped appearance.
Prefer sentence case for navigation and labels instead of all caps, except for tiny overline labels.
Use tabular-nums font feature for financial tables and numeric columns to ensure alignment.

charts_and_graphs.description: Guidelines for data visualization components including bar charts, line charts, pie/donut charts, and color palettes for data series.
general_principles: Prioritize clarity: charts should communicate insights at a glance without clutter.
Use minimal gridlines and axis decoration; let the data speak.
Default to monochrome or neutral palettes, introducing accent colors only for emphasis.
Maintain consistent spacing and padding within chart containers.
Ensure all text labels are legible using body.xs or body.sm typography tokens.

bar_chart.description: Vertical or horizontal bar charts for comparing discrete categories or time-series data.

bar_style.bar_width: Auto-calculated with 40–60% category width, maintaining spacing.2 gap between bars.
bar_style.hover_style: Slightly darken fill or add subtle shadow.

y_axis.gridlines: Horizontal only, using color.border.subtle with reduced opacity (0.5).

legend.color_indicator: Small square or circle (8×8px) matching bar color.

line_chart.description: Line charts for showing trends over time or continuous data.

data_points.show: On hover or for key milestones only

area_fill.fill_color: Gradient from line color at 20% opacity to transparent
area_fill.usage: Use sparingly to highlight primary series.

pie_donut_chart.description: Pie or donut charts for showing part-to-whole relationships.

segment_style.hover_style: Slightly scale segment outward or increase brightness.

donut_hole.center_content: Optional: display total value or key metric in numeric.lg style.

legend.layout: Vertical list with color indicator (circle, 8px) and label with percentage.

color_palette_for_data.description: Recommended color sequences for multi-series charts.
color_palette_for_data.usage: Default to monochrome for single-category data. Use categorical palette only when distinguishing multiple unrelated series.

sparklines.description: Tiny inline charts for showing trends in compact spaces (e.g., table cells).
sparklines.usage: No axes or labels; purely visual trend indicator.

tooltips.description: Hover tooltips for displaying detailed data points.
tooltips.content: Show data label, value, and optional context (e.g., date, percentage).

app_shell.description: The main container that holds sidebar, header (if used), and content grid.
app_shell.layout: Sidebar fixed to the left, content area to the right with a light canvas background. Content is centered with maximum width and equal outer margins.

sidebar.description: Vertical navigation with logo, search, nav items, utility links, and user profile.

top_nav.description: Optional horizontal header bar that can host breadcrumbs, date range selectors, and global actions.
top_nav.background: Transparent over canvas or subtle gradient; keep minimal.
top_nav.alignment: Left-aligned title, right-aligned actions such as profile icon or notifications.

card.description: Primary surface for grouped content such as metrics, charts, and summaries.

header.layout: Title on left, optional actions (date range dropdown, menu icon) on right.

body.layout: Flexible. Use consistent vertical rhythm and align numbers and labels on a common baseline.

profile_summary_card.description: Card with user avatar, name, role, and short description.
profile_summary_card.layout: Avatar on the left, with name and role stacked to the right. Below, a paragraph of copy describing the user.

stat_summary_card.description: Compact cards showing short descriptive text and key financial metrics.
stat_summary_card.layout: Title at top, short descriptive paragraph, key numeric value aligned at bottom or right side.
stat_summary_card.interaction: Static or with subtle hover elevation increase.

investment_summary_card.description: Complex card displaying headline figure, category selector, and supporting table/list.
sections: Top row: card title and optional chip indicating state (e.g., 'Desired duration').
Hero numeric: large dollar value in numeric.lg style.
Control row: dropdown for category selection, summary badges for options like 'Available cash assets'.
Data list or table: rows with category name, amount, and time indication.

controls.dropdown_style: bordered subtle input with chevron, radius.md, neutral background.
controls.chips: Pill-shaped, soft border, subtle background using accent or neutral soft colors.

chart_card.description: Card containing bar charts or pie/donut charts with minimal chrome.
chart_card.layout: Header with title and date range selector, body with chart, footer with short legend or summary.

chart_area.axis_style: Minimal axis lines using color.border.subtle and small labels in body.sm.
chart_area.bar_style: Solid bars in dark monochrome (color.chart.bar_primary) with rounded top corners.
chart_area.pie_style: Donut segments with dark, mid, and light neutrals; slight separation between segments.

legend.layout: Right-aligned descriptions with colored bullets or small squares matching chart colors.

data_table.description: Simple, clean table for financial breakdowns.

cell.alignment: Use left alignment for labels and right alignment for numeric values.

button.description: Used sparingly; primary actions like 'View Full Report'.

primary.hover: Darken the background slightly and increase shadow subtly.

badge.description: Small pill-style labels used for statuses, durations, and category chips.

input.description: Base form input style used for search, date range, and dropdown triggers.

dropdown.description: Used for date range and category selection. Visually similar to input with right-aligned chevron.
dropdown.trigger_style: Same as input with optional subtle background in color.background.card_muted.

iconography.description: Simple, line-based icons with consistent stroke width.
guidelines: Use lightweight icons that do not overpower typography.
Align icons tightly with text labels in navigation and buttons.
Avoid complex or overly illustrative icons; favor simple, geometric shapes.

avatars.description: Circular avatars used for user profile sections.
avatars.border: Optional thin white border when placed over colored backgrounds.

status_indicators.description: Tiny dots or icons that indicate positive/negative trends or completion.

design_principles: Clarity over decoration: Every visual element should support understanding of financial data or navigation clarity.
Hierarchy through structure: Rely on layout, spacing, and type hierarchy to guide attention rather than heavy borders or bright colors.
Soft contrast: Use soft background contrasts and subtle shadows to create depth, avoiding harsh outlines.
Monochrome-first charts: Default charts to a mostly monochrome palette, introducing accent colors only for emphasis and key series.
Consistency in spacing: Use the defined spacing scale everywhere. Misaligned or inconsistent gaps should be treated as bugs.
Information density with breathing room: Present many metrics and cards on screen, but maintain enough whitespace that nothing feels cramped.
Minimal motion: If animations are added, keep them subtle and utilitarian (e.g., fade/slide on hover or load) rather than flashy.
Accessible contrast: Maintain sufficient contrast for text and key data points, especially in charts and small labels.
Predictable interactions: Buttons, inputs, and dropdowns should behave consistently across the app, with familiar hover and focus states.
